<thought>Based on the mass spectrum (M≈268 Da) and the 13C NMR (12 aromatic carbons appearing in pairs and 6 aliphatic carbons also in pairs), the compound likely consists of two identical aromatic halves each bearing a propoxy substituent. A plausible structure is 4,4′‑bis(propoxy)biphenyl, whose SMILES is “c1ccc(cc1OCC(C))c2ccc(cc2OCC(C))”. This matches the symmetry (each carbon type appears twice) and the carbon count (18 C).</thought>
<final_answer>c1ccc(cc1OCC(C))c2ccc(cc2OCC(C))</final_answer>
